newsitem.title: FINLAND: Turkish mining industry needs to grow-miner.
newsitem.headline: Turkish mining industry needs to grow-miner.

text.p: Turkey's copper and zinc mining industries need to grow to fulfill expanding domestic needs, but current reserves are insufficient or hard to access, a senior mining official told delegates of the Metal Bulletin base metal concentrates conference on Thursday.

Blister copper consumption is currently at 130,000 tonnes and growing, but 100,000 tonnes are being imported annually, said Faik Yilmaz Sener, investment project manager from Turkey's Cinkur Zinc-Lead industry.
Meanwhile, copper concentrate output last year was 240,000 tonnes but the surplus from a limited domestic smelting capacity -- 117,085 tonnes -- was exported.
"In order to meet the growing demand for blister copper in Turkey, expansion in existing capacities and/or new greenfield smelter constructions are necessary," Sener said.
But existing deposits with known reserves will not be sufficient to meet growing demand and more exploration is required, he added.

Total known reserves, based on 6.4 percent zinc, 1.72 percent lead and 2.9 percent copper, is estimated at about 55.5 million tonnes -- equivalent to a metal content of 3.6 million tonnes zinc, 96,000 tonnes lead and 1.6 million tonnes copper.
Turkish mine production totalled 4.8 million tonnes last year with an average grade of 1.4 percent copper.
Similarly, annual demand for zinc is 60,000 tonnes and forecast to reach 70,000 by 2000, he said. Cinkur, Turkey's sole zinc metal producer last year produced 24,000 tonnes.

The biggest producer of zinc concentrate, Cayeli Copper Inc., produced 80,000 tonnes of concentrate last year. It plans to invest $25 million to increase annual output to 125,000 tonnes copper concentrate and 80,000 tonnes zinc concentrate.
Besides Cayeli, however, there are no reserves big enought to warrant mechnisation and automation, and most are found in remote locations at higher altitudes..
Canada's Cominco Mining Co, meanwhile, is expected to start production in 1997-98 at a deposit in Artvin with reserves of 4.1 million tonnes assaying 4.9 percent copper.
Copper miner Etibank is seeking a partner to develop a deposit with 14.5 million tonne reserve.
